collab.question: Design the `Source` class for the site's source library: one web page an agent found (documentation, source code on GitHub, an article), already converted to markdown and saved once under public/framework/sources/<topic>/, listed in an index.jsonl there, so any other agent can read it quickly and cite it. It needs at least: the url, what kind of page it is, how authoritative it is, and the path of its markdown file. House style: plain ES classes, assign-based constructors (`constructor(o){ Object.assign(this, o) }`), small methods, parts as static subclasses. Read public/framework/ai/2026/09/28/agent-work-on-every-page-sanity-checks-c/design.md (the 'Added' section) for where it fits.

msg: Proposed Source class: properties (url, kind, authority, path, title), methods (constructor, markdown, cite, isValid), static subclasses (Kind and Authority)

decision.ask: Which whole signature set for Source (class name, properties, methods and their arguments)?

options.say: haiku-c: # Source Class Design — Object Structure Proposal

msg: Voted for sonnet-b: complete lifecycle methods (fetch, save, load, list), rich metadata (fetchedBy, fetchedAt), Authority.guess() normalization, sizeOf/exists() catch errors

vote.caveat: Authority as 0–1 scale is powerful but ambiguous without defaults; clarify what 0.5 means (neutral? medium? 50% trustworthy?) so all agents interpret it the same way.

fetch() is ambitious—if network/markdown conversion becomes unwieldy, move it to a separate Fetcher class and keep Source as the data model; as proposed, though, sonnet-b covers the full workflow agents need
add a static Source.load(topic) / instance save() pair so the class itself knows how to read and append its own index.jsonl row, instead of leaving all file I/O to an unspecified external loader

msg: Implemented Source class per sonnet-b spec: 9 properties, 2 static subclasses (KINDS array, Authority.guess), 8 async methods (fetch, save, load, list, exists, sizeOf, cite)
Cross-reviewed: sonnet-b elegant but Authority.guess lacks URL patterns and Markdown.from() is broken; haiku-c more complete (realistic Authority, real HTML→markdown) but has Math.min bug
Final vote: haiku-c—more complete (URL patterns work, HTML→markdown implemented) despite Math.min bug; sonnet-b elegant but core logic broken (no URL analysis, Markdown returns HTML)

decision.ask: Which implementation of the winning signature is best?

msg: Final vote: haiku-c—actually converts HTML, attempts domain analysis; sonnet-b's Markdown.from() returns HTML unchanged, Authority.guess flat. Caveat: haiku-c's allowlist is brittle, needs pattern approach

vote.caveat: Adopt haiku-a's title extraction fallbacks (og:title, h1 tag) into Source.Markdown.titleOf() to recover titles from more pages in production.

haiku-c's Authority.guess domain allowlist is brittle and will silently default to 0.50 for most unknown docs sites; should switch to a domain-pattern approach like haiku-a's (includes + tier adjustments) to be extensible
